The Public Relations Officer of the Borno State Police Command, ASP Nahum Daso, says stranded travellers can approach the nearest police station for help. The PPRO, in a post on his official Facebook page on Thursday, said the police were not only there to enforce the law but also to protect, guide and assist the people. Daso cited a recent incident in which police officers in Kano State assisted a stranded traveller who left Maiduguri to visit her relatives but lost contact with them upon arrival. The post reads: “What would you do if you travelled to another city and suddenly became stranded, with no phone, no address and no one to turn to? “A lady travelled from Maiduguri to Kano to visit her relatives. Unfortunately, she became stranded and missing, with no mobile phone to contact anyone and no knowledge of her relatives’ residential address,” he said. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources The PPRO stated that, in a remarkable demonstration of compassion and professionalism, police officers intervened, established contact with the relevant authorities in her home state, traced her family in Maiduguri and facilitated her safe return home. “Here is an important safety reminder: If you ever find yourself lost, stranded or in distress, don’t hesitate to approach the nearest police station. Help is available,” he said. “The Police are not only there to enforce the law, they are also there to protect, guide and assist,” he added. NDC reinstates Borno candidate after Atiku campaign controversy Liatu Dawa: Faith sharing is not a crime CAN confirms appeal of Borno woman’s conviction The PPRO urged travellers to always inform a trusted family member or friend about their travel plans, destination and expected arrival time. “Establish contact with who you are visiting and ensure they confirm their availability. Write down the full address and contact details of the person you are visiting,” he said. “Keep your identification card and some emergency money safely with you. If you become stranded or lost: Stay calm and avoid wandering into unfamiliar or isolated areas. Approach the nearest Police Station or identifiable Police officers and explain your situation,” he added. He also urged travellers in such situations to seek assistance from recognised transport authorities or other responsible public officials. “Try to remember or provide any available details about your relatives, destination or emergency contacts. Avoid sharing sensitive personal information or accepting suspicious offers of help from strangers,” Daso stressed. Isah Ojo
